China’s five-year government bond yield dropped to a record low after the central bank increased its cash injection into the banking system.

A rally in Wall Street tech stocks following Anthropic PBC’s filing for an initial public offering carried into Asia, rekindling enthusiasm for the artificial intelligence trade. Crude oil extended its decline.
South Korea’s Kospi Index — a barometer for the AI trade — jumped 4.5%, with chip heavyweights SK Hynix Inc. and Samsung Electronics Co. climbing. Semiconductor stocks also rallied in Japan, helping lift the broader MSCI Asia Pacific Index 1%.

The yen’s funding role for the carry trade in Latin America is alive and well.
While the Brazilian real slumped against the Japanese currency following the reelection of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, others in the region gained, including the Chilean peso, Colombian peso and the Mexican peso. That underscored continued demand for Latin American currencies that have been key destinations to invest money borrowed in Japan.

Asian semiconductor stocks jumped, as Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering filing helped renew investor enthusiasm for the artificial intelligence trade.
Shares of Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc. climbed more than 5% each in early trading, pushing South Korea’s equity benchmark Kospi up as much as 4.5%. Japan’s Nikkei 225 Stock Average rose as much as 2.4%, with chip-related Advantest Corp. and Sumco Corp. up more than 5% each. Taiwan’s Taiex rose more than 1% before paring its gain.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Universal Music Group, the world’s largest record company, has discussed going private with a few prominent Wall Street firms, according to people familiar with the matter.
Universal’s management held preliminary conversations with private equity firms including Apollo Global Management Inc., TPG Inc. and Blackstone Inc. earlier this year, said the people, who asked not to to be identified because the talks were confidential. The board of the company, with a market value of €29 billion ($32 billion), is aware of the discussions, they added.

Oil declined for a second day — pulling further back from a six-month high — as stepped-up diplomatic efforts strengthened expectations that a broader escalation in the US-Iran war may be averted.
Brent dropped toward $115 a barrel after losing almost 1% in the previous session, while West Texas Intermediate traded near $101. Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey traveled to Tehran for discussions on Monday, with participants agreeing to continue talks, IRIB news agency reported.

Bank Indonesia may need to deploy more aggressive measures, including further rate hikes, to sustainably lift the rupiah from near-record lows, according to analysts.
Indonesia’s central bank pledgedBloomberg Terminal
last week to make “necessary adjustments” to its policy tools to maintain rupiah stability as elevated global yields, rising oil prices and the risk of losing its emerging-market status under MSCI Inc. spur foreign outflows. BI had kept its key rate at 5.75%, opting for currency intervention and hedging incentives over monetary tightening that could weigh on the economy.

item.title: Dave Lee: Anthropic Brings ‘Anti-Sell’ Strategy to Its IPO
item.description:
BusinessWeek Radio Simulcast • Oct 26th, 2026
Dave Lee: Anthropic Brings ‘Anti-Sell’ Strategy to Its IPO
Dave Lee, Bloomberg Opinion US Technology Columnist, joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss his piece about Anthropic's IPO announcement. Lee writes about the firm's S-1 containing warnings about the company and prospects for humanity as AI technology continues to advance. Lee adds that the filing is described as “a pitch deliberately designed to be unappealing to those who are a poor fit … while appealing to the type of person we want to hire.” Lee speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Anthropic PBC warned it may need to seek more financing sooner than the artificial-intelligence company had anticipated while saying little about its potential path to an investment-grade credit rating in its closely watched IPO filing.
Reaching investment grade could give the maker of Claude access to a much deeper pool of capital at a time when its funding requirements are ballooning. Insurance companies, pension funds and other large investors are major buyers of high-grade corporate bonds, and attaining those ratings could allow Anthropic to borrow more cheaply.

item.title: Duke’s Mayo CEO: Our Room for Growth Is Substantial
item.description: E. Yuri Hermida, CEO of Duke’s Mayo Company, discussed the company’s name change from Sauer Brands as it enters a new growth chapter. After divesting its spice business, the company is centering its identity on Duke’s Mayo, whose heritage and recipe date to 1917, while also owning Mateo’s Gourmet Salsa. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
